summary: San Francisco society astrologer Joan Quigley secretly set the timing of Ronald Reagan's speeches, flights, debates and summits for Nancy Reagan from 1981 to 1988, then claimed credit for the era's successes in a memoir.

evidence.note: born in Kansas City in 1927; San Francisco upbringing and early career follow
White House working relationship begins after the March 1981 assassination attempt
Donald Regan's 1988 memoir exposes her role, ending the secret arrangement
her 1990 memoir is the main source, but the episode is narrated as a career history
she claims she rebuilt Nancy Reagan's public image and steered her away from fashion press
claims she pushed Nancy toward the anti-drug crusade; drug war incarceration discussed
timed press conferences, debates with Carter and Mondale, and Air Force One flights
1985 Bitburg cemetery visit in West Germany, timed by her astrology
claims role in Gorbachev relations, Reykjavik summit and INF treaty signing time

notes: Episode leans heavily on Quigley's memoir but is told as a career history, so deep-dive rather than media-reading.
